framework_note: Performance scenarios use time.perf_counter() + statistics — same pattern as S2 ST-004 (test_perf_apply_inward.py). The /ases-system-test skill template suggests pytest-benchmark, but the project venv doesn't have it installed and S2 already established the perf_counter idiom. Adding a backend dep mid-Phase-3 needs PO approval; consistency with S2 wins.

scenarios.nfr_ref: PRD non_functional.performance — 'Dashboard sub-second for single date'
scenarios.risk_ref: HLD R-002 (dashboard SUM scales with volume — mitigated by DS-003 materialized ledger)
scenarios.description: Sustained p95 latency of GET /api/v1/dashboard under realistic catalog (6 active design-grade pairs) × 12 months of accumulated ledger (~2016 rows). Distinct from the unit-level TC-122 perf gate at the service layer — this measures the FULL HTTP stack (TestClient → router → DI → service → repo → testcontainers PG).
scenarios.threshold_rationale: PRD says 'sub-second' (< 1000ms). 800ms gives 20% headroom over the spec and is consistent with the same '< 500ms' service-level target from TC-122 (network + serialization overhead is well under 300ms on a testcontainer).

scenarios.nfr_ref: PRD non_functional.performance — 'Sales Report < 2s for 1 year of data unfiltered'
scenarios.description: Sustained p95 latency of GET /api/v1/reports/sales with NO filters over a realistic year of sales: 6 dealers × 12 months × 50 sales/month × 3 lines/sale ≈ 10,800 sales_line rows. Verifies the LLD's claim that the consolidation + transactions queries — both running against the existing S2 composite indexes (ix_sales_header_sales_date, ix_sales_line_dgd) — stay under the 2s budget through the full HTTP stack.

SQL-injection protection across ALL THREE list-type filters of GET /reports/sales: dealer_ids (list[int] — typed at parse time), places (list[str] — typed but free-form), design_ids (list[int]). Extends TC-158 which only covered places. For typed-int filters, sending a SQL-payload string is expected to 422 at FastAPI's Query parsing layer. For places (free-form string), the injection payload is bound through SQLAlchemy .in_() and matches no real rows.

injections.rationale: FastAPI rejects non-int values; never reaches the service
.in_() parameter binding causes the literal string to match no place_snapshot value

scenarios.post_assertion: After all 3 injection attempts, the tbl_sales_header table still exists and still has the seeded rows — confirming the DROP attempts were not executed.

scenarios.risk_ref: HLD R-004 — V1 has no auth (mitigation: deployment on trusted network only; documented as DS-005)
scenarios.description: Verify the V1 no-auth posture is consistently applied to the 2 NEW S3 endpoints (mirroring S1 ST-002 which already covered S1+S2 endpoints). Both GET /api/v1/dashboard and GET /api/v1/reports/sales must accept requests WITHOUT any Authorization header — V1 is intentionally open on a trusted network. If auth ever gets added in V2, these tests must be updated/removed (currently they ASSERT no-auth).
assertions: GET /api/v1/dashboard?as_of_date=<today> returns 200 with no Authorization header
GET /api/v1/dashboard?as_of_date=<today> still returns 200 even with a bogus Authorization header (FastAPI ignores unconfigured auth)
GET /api/v1/reports/sales returns 200 with no Authorization header
GET /api/v1/reports/sales returns 200 with a bogus Authorization header

scenarios.risk_ref: HLD R-005 — soft-delete of design-grade mapping with existing transactions (mitigation: is_active=false; reports JOIN against masters and display historical grade_code)
scenarios.description: End-to-end soft-delete behavior: a (design, grade) pair has historical ledger rows from prior transactions. The mapping is then deactivated (map.is_active=False). The dashboard MUST exclude this pair from the row-set going forward (DesignGradeMapRepository.list_active_all only returns active rows), even though historical ledger data still exists for the pair. Independently, the Sales Report must still return transactions that reference the deactivated pair (historical fidelity — joining on FK with no is_active filter on tbl_sales_line).

test_data.expected_sales_report_after_deactivation: the historical sale row IS in response (transactions[] AND consolidation[] include the deactivated pair via FK join)

boundary_values: map.is_active=False after deactivation (pair hidden from dashboard, still shown in sales report)

execution_results.details: GET /api/v1/dashboard p95=33.1ms over 30 samples; 2016 ledger rows seeded with per-pair cumulative running_balance. ~24x headroom vs PRD 'sub-second' threshold.

GET /api/v1/reports/sales (no filters) p95=715.7ms over 15 samples; 10,800 sales_line rows seeded. ~2.8x headroom vs PRD 2s threshold. DS-017 shared-predicate + ix_sales_* indexes keep both queries within budget.

All 3 injection payloads neutralized: dealer_ids/design_ids → 422 (FastAPI int parse); places → 200 with empty results (SQLAlchemy .in_() binding). Post-loop confirmation: tbl_sales_header still has seed row.
4/4 GETs return 200 — V1 no-auth contract verified for both new S3 endpoints.

3-phase E2E: (a) active pair → closing=80; (b) is_active=False → pair hidden from dashboard; (c) historical SalesLine for deactivated pair → still present in /reports/sales consolidation + transactions. R-005 mitigation verified.
